Continuation terminal is a85055a718cdbe67d8b780164edc6e36021d7f42 at 22842.617236 us aggregate and 74554.319 us n2048. The guard-admissible protocol assigns the synchronized optimized n2048 route to the first Python thread and serializes every non-owner caller through torch.linalg.eigh under the same execution lock, with device completion before ownership handoff. Kernelguard is clean, the source has no forbidden execution-context keyword, official validation is 39/39, and three repeated rounds of four simultaneously released separate-context callers covering two dense and two mixed n2048 inputs all passed the frozen checker. Forced poisoned-handle, status1, unavailable-capability, old-header/dlsym compatibility, BF16x9-disabled, and BF16x9-plus-grouped-disabled modes each built clean and passed 39/39, measuring 23160.660221, 23177.779002, 23185.494919, 22863.747160, 23191.115476, and 23181.563775 us. Boundary-only device completion failed mixed residuals; whole-call locking still failed because custom state migrated across contexts; even final completion failed on the fourth sequential context; owner routing without fallback serialization raced the PyTorch lazy cuSOLVER wrapper. The final owner plus serialized fallback design resolved all of those cases. The exact validation command completed inside an explicit 240-second envelope in 7.627 seconds after acquisition. A clean compile took about 65.636 seconds, so compile plus test is about 73.3 seconds; the public 240-second timeout was not reproducible. The only long observation was a 646.809-second fleet-lock wait outside command execution and outside the explicit timeout. Terminal Nsight Systems profile is tied to the exact SHA; the resident n2048 reducer remains 86.3 percent of GPU kernel time at 63.623 ms average, leaving it as the main performance target. No leaderboard submission was made. Follow-on openings are a guard-admissible per-call all-C++ route that removes device-wide completion, truly context-local raw solver state without forbidden APIs, or independently initialized raw cuSolver fallback handles to replace serialized torch.linalg while preserving four-caller correctness.

Further measurable openings include a thread-local isolated solver cache to remove repeated handle/workspace setup, testing isolated BF16x9 cuSOLVER math against the frozen checker to lower fallback latency, and an all-C++ ownership dispatcher that can safely grant the optimized route beyond the Python main thread without reintroducing device-wide completion or forbidden APIs.
